criteria.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs builds VerdictInputs with passing checks reused from CI (exit_code None, reused field set, same tree and commit) and a behavior criterion citing `cargo test`, and asserts the criterion is met with commands_verified true. Run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`; the test passes, and it fails on the base code (judge() ignores records without exit code 0).
criteria.evidence: I ran this. `verify::tests::a_passing_check_reused_from_ci_on_the_same_commit_counts_as_run` passed (69 passed, 0 failed). The test calls judge() through judge_recorded with a record that has exit_code None, reused true and passed true, with candidate_tree = checks_tree = "abc" and the cited command `cargo test`. It asserts criteria[1].met, commands_verified and no D43 finding. It also covers fmt and clippy by their command text. On the base code the filter was `c.passed && c.exit_code == Some(0)` (seen in the diff), which drops this record, so the assertions would fail. The test also needs the new field, so it would not even compile on the base.

criteria.criterion: Unit tests in verify.rs show a reused record for a different commit/tree, a failed reused record, and a skipped record each leave the `cargo test` behavior criterion unmet. Run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`.
criteria.evidence: I ran this. Three tests passed. `a_check_reused_from_ci_for_another_commit_does_not_count_as_run` covers checks_tree "def" and None. `a_failed_check_reused_from_ci_does_not_count_as_run` and `a_skipped_check_that_was_not_reused_does_not_count_as_run` cover the other two cases. Each asserts !met, !commands_verified and that a D43 finding exists. The existing test `a_placeholder_record_without_an_exit_code_does_not_count_as_run` still passes.

criteria.criterion: CheckRun in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs gains a serde-defaulted boolean field marking reused records (not note-text matching), crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs sets it where reused records are built, and judge() reads the field, not the note string (Grep for the note text in verify.rs finds no matching on it).
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: records.rs adds `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")] pub reused: bool`. checks.rs sets `reused: true` only in runs_from_record; skipped, local and baseline records set false. judge() filters on `c.reused && c.exit_code.is_none()`. I grepped verify.rs for 'result reused|note': the only hit for the note text is in the test fixture (line 749), and judge() does not match on the note. The checks.rs producer test (`a_record_for_the_same_sha_stands_in_for_the_checks_and_another_sha_does_not`, which now asserts every CI-built record is reused) and all 22 routing tests passed when I ran them.

criteria.criterion: A records.rs test deserializes a CheckRun JSON without the new field and it loads with the field false, and a reused record round-trips through check_record_file/AnyRecord. Run `cargo test -p athena-data`.
criteria.evidence: I ran this: 142 passed, 0 failed. `a_check_run_written_before_reuse_was_marked_loads_as_not_reused` serialises an unreused record, asserts the JSON has no `reused` key, then deserialises it with reused == false. `a_reused_check_record_round_trips_and_validates` sets reused true, round-trips the record through AnyRecord::to_json/parse, and asserts check_record_file(...baseline.json) is Ok.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing that checks reused from a green CI run for the candidate commit now count as commands run in the verdict (D43, D115).
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: a new bullet under [Unreleased] / Fixed says exactly this, names D43 and D115, gives the root cause (judge counted only records with exit code 0, and CI records have none), describes the new optional `reused` field, and lists the cases that still do not count.

findings.summary: Six changed files are not on the expected deliverables list. Each change is a one-line `reused: false` in a CheckRun struct literal.
findings.evidence: The diff stat lists these files, but the expected deliverables do not. Each adds only `reused: false`, which the code needs to compile once the field exists (CheckRun has no Default). They appear in the planned files list. The scope is unavoidable and adds no behavior.

summary: The change does what the request asks, so the verdict is pass. The verdict stage (`judge()`) had counted only check records with exit code 0 as commands seen running. Results reused from CI carry no exit code, so they never counted, and passing jobs were rejected under D43. Now a record marked with a new `reused` field also counts if it passed and has no exit code, under the same guard as before: the checks ran on the candidate commit. The fix is at the root, in that counting rule. The code that builds reused records (`checks::runs_from_record`) sets the field, and only for the candidate commit, because it returns nothing for any other commit. In production the guard compares the candidate commit with itself (seen in run/verification.rs:336-338). Failed, skipped, placeholder and other-commit records still do not count, and tests show each case. Older records without the field load as not reused, and a reused record round-trips and passes record validation. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core verify` (69 passed), `cargo test -p athena-data` (142 passed), the checks.rs reuse test and the routing tests (22 passed); all pass. The CHANGELOG entry is present and accurate. The one finding is minor: six files outside the deliverables list each gained only `reused: false`, which the code needs to compile now that the field exists. All of this was run on the snapshot in my working directory, not the real repository.
